label: X25519
ipg_usage: Ephemeral sender key agreement with the recipient public key inside the native envelope suite

label: HKDF-SHA-256
ipg_usage: Derive the envelope encryption key from the X25519 shared secret with protocol context

label: ChaCha20-Poly1305
ipg_usage: Protect envelope plaintext and wrapped private seeds; authenticate before releasing plaintext
limitations: Nonce reuse under the same key is unsafe
Ciphertext authentication is not proof of sender identity

label: Ed25519
ipg_usage: Domain-separated content signatures and signed identity lifecycle certificates
limitations: Key identity needs an independent trust binding

label: Argon2id
ipg_usage: Derive private-key wrapping keys using the fixed IPG v1 profile: 65536 KiB memory, 3 iterations, 4 lanes
limitations: IPG profile is a protocol choice, not a universal password policy

label: SHA-256
ipg_usage: File digests, ipg-public-v1 fingerprints and legacy v1/v2 trust snapshot digests
limitations: Unkeyed hashing does not prove origin
Fast hashing is not password hardening

label: ECDH P-384
ipg_usage: Ephemeral sender key agreement with a P-384 identity; tokens run CKM_ECDH1_DERIVE, preferably with the X9.63 KDF so the shared secret never leaves them
limitations: Points must be validated uncompressed curve points

label: AES-256-GCM
ipg_usage: Protect P-384 envelope plaintext; authenticate before releasing plaintext
limitations: Nonce reuse under the same key is catastrophic
Ciphertext authentication is not proof of sender identity

label: ECDSA P-384 with SHA-384
ipg_usage: Hardware identity signatures, certificates and possession checks; tokens sign the SHA-384 digest with CKM_ECDSA and IPG canonicalizes to low-s
limitations: Signatures are malleable unless low-s is enforced, which IPG does

label: SHA-384
ipg_usage: P-384 and hybrid identity fingerprints, ipg-trust-v3 snapshot digests, the message digest for ECDSA P-384 signatures, and the hash inside the P-384 envelope's ANSI X9.63 KDF (PKCS#11 CKD_SHA384_KDF) and its SharedInfo commitment
limitations: No standalone IPG sha2-384 digest command

label: ML-KEM-768
ipg_usage: Encapsulates a second shared secret to hybrid identities; combined with X25519 by HKDF so either component alone protects the envelope
limitations: Encapsulation only, not encryption or authentication
Marked experimental in IronCrypto; interoperability checked against PyCA and OpenSSL

label: ML-DSA-65
ipg_usage: Second half of composite ed25519-mldsa65 signatures and certificates for hybrid identities; hedged signing with a fixed IPG context string
limitations: Used only in composite with Ed25519
Marked experimental in IronCrypto; interoperability checked against PyCA and OpenSSL
